task.task_name: Triage a personal auto collision claim
task.task_description: You handle new auto insurance claims. A policyholder reports a two-car collision at an intersection and sends in their account of what happened, vehicle details, damage photos, the other driver's contact and insurance information, and a police report number. Some details might be missing or conflicting, and there may not be a repair estimate yet. Your task is to check the claim against the policy and available records, see whether there's enough information to move it forward, flag missing documents or possible coverage issues, and send it to the right claims team. Straightforward claims can go through the usual process. Claims involving injuries, conflicting accounts, signs of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions need specialist attention. You're getting the claim ready for an adjuster, who will make the final coverage and liability decisions.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Review the reported collision and submitted evidence
operational_subtasks.description: Review the policyholder’s account, vehicle and party details, damage photos, other driver’s information, and police report reference to establish the reported incident facts and identify apparent gaps or inconsistencies in those materials.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume this review occurs once for every claim. Reviewing several submitted items and reconciling their facts takes moderate effort; the task provides the expected types of materials but no measured review time.

operational_subtasks.description: Review the applicable policy and available claim or incident records to check relevant policy details, the reported vehicle and parties, and the incident date against the reported collision; identify apparent coverage discrepancies without making the adjuster’s final coverage decision.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one policy-and-record check per claim. Comparing claim facts with policy terms and any available records can require more effort than reviewing the submission alone, especially when details do not align; actual record availability is unspecified.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Assess whether claim information is sufficient to proceed
operational_subtasks.description: Determine whether the information and documents available are sufficient to move the claim forward, and identify missing or unclear details or documents, including whether a repair estimate is needed at this stage.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one sufficiency assessment per claim. Most reviews are expected to involve a straightforward comparison with information needed for claim handling; identifying and evaluating missing or unclear items adds effort when gaps are present, with their rate unspecified.

operational_subtasks.description: Assess the claim information and available records for reported injuries, conflicting accounts, signs of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions that warrant specialist attention.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume every claim receives one screen. A closer evaluation of a trigger is conditional; as a model-generated assumption, 10–30% of claims may need additional review of one or more flags, increasing effort per claim when that occurs.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Communicate triage findings and route the claim
operational_subtasks.description: Send the claim to the usual claims team or the appropriate specialist team, communicating the reported facts, any missing information or documents, and apparent coverage concerns for the adjuster’s review.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one handoff per claim. Routing and conveying a concise summary are generally limited-effort tasks, with somewhat more coordination when specialist attention or unresolved issues need to be highlighted.
